text:
alex: Heads up — prototype to move inference runtime from collector-agent -> direct OTLP export. Need a short list of "best-practice" patterns for multi-lang SDK init, graceful handoff, per-tenant sampling, and exporter backpressure. Anyone seen nasty edge cases?

maria: We ran into double-send when teams forgot to disable the agent while enabling direct export. Quick rule: single source of truth for export (toggle) + override service.name so ingest can dedupe. :warning:

tony: Per-tenant sampling question: SDK-side sampler (tenant header) vs server-side sampler at ingest. Which do we prefer for inference workloads?

sophia: SDK-side reduces ingest cost but is easy to bypass if clients misconfigure. Server-side guarantees policy enforcement. We usually do hybrid: conservative SDK sampling (reduce noise) + server-side enforced sampling/retention for compliance. :thinking_face:

ryan: Python starter snippet I used for graceful init/shutdown (keeps BSP flush on SIGTERM):

```python
import os
import signal
from opentelemetry import trace
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor
from opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.grpc.trace_exporter import OTLPSpanExporter

endpoint = os.getenv("OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT", "https://otel-ingest.internal")
exporter = OTLPSpanExporter(endpoint=endpoint, headers=("x-tenant-id", os.getenv("TENANT_ID", "default")))
provider = TracerProvider()
provider.add_span_processor(BatchSpanProcessor(exporter))
trace.set_tracer_provider(provider)

# on SIGTERM -> provider.shutdown() to flush
```

maria: In Rust we spawn a tokio task that awaits tracer.shutdown() on signal; set OTEL_BSP_EXPORT_TIMEOUT_MS high enough for large batches. Also ensure collector connection is non-blocking so process can exit gracefully.

tony: Go gotcha: otlptracehttp vs otlptracegrpc — grpc preserves trailer metadata we sometimes rely on for tenant attribution. For multi-tenant, we set per-exporter headers: `headers := map[string]string{"x-tenant-id": tenant}` and create one client per-tenant or a middleware that injects header per request. Example: 

```go
exporter, _ := otlptracegrpc.New(ctx, otlptracegrpc.WithEndpoint(endpoint), otlptracegrpc.WithHeaders(map[string]string{"x-tenant-id": tenant}))
provider := sdktrace.NewTracerProvider(sdktrace.WithBatcher(exporter))
```

alex: Another operational Q — we want to retain full spans for errors and aggregate/short-TTL for KV cache hits. How do folks tag and route those cheaply?

sophia: Add a stable attribute e.g. `redwood.inference.path="kv-hit"` or `redwood.telemetry.hot_path=true` at the span creation point. In collector pipeline, have a routing rule that rewrites retention and sends hot_path spans to a cheaper hot-tier (shorter TTL + aggregate metrics). Need naming conventions documented.

ryan: Prefer not to bake routing logic into every SDK. Let SDK set a small set of semantics attributes and let collector/ingest rewrite or annotate before retention decisions. TraceState is an option but attribute-based routing is simpler.

maria: Also watch SDK memory under backpressure: enable bounded BSP queue and drop behavior. For Python/Go set a small queue_size and drop_oldest=True or block with a fairness policy. This avoids OOM when backend spikes. :thumbsup:

dev-ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: otel-direct-export enabled for 5% inference traffic in eu-west1 (2026-03-19T18:45Z).

alex: Great — I'll draft a short RFC: include (1) SDK init snippets for py/go/rust, (2) collector routing sample for hot-path retention, (3) canary checklist (traffic %, failover to agent, metrics to watch). Will ping for review tomorrow. Thanks all!
